title.point: God guides His people. We can be those who follow our parents, serving ones, and older ones regarding where to go and what to do.

thisWeekSong.title: Move with God, Wherever He Leads Us

lyricsLeft.text: Move with God, wherever He leads us,
Move with God, wherever He guides.
Move with God, He knows where He needs us,
Move with God, however He guides.
Obeyed God to follow His call.

lyricsRight.text: God told Moses, “Go out of Egypt,
Take My people out of that place.
Build the house in the way that I tell you,
Follow Me in all that I say.”
Mom and Dad, now follow God’s leading,
We’re on earth to move on with Him.
He will show us how we should follow,
Just obey in all that He speaks.

lastWeekSong.title: I Can Find Among God's People

lyrics.text:
I can find among God’s people
the companionships I need.
I can find care and protection
with those in God’s family.

Oh, how wonderful, I’m not alone,
God’s people care for me!
With God’s people I’ll stay.

I was born among God’s people.
Not alone, I’m with God’s people.
I’m protected with God’s people.
With God’s people I’ll stay.

lastWeekReview.title: Being Formed into an Army
bullets: Israel was getting ready to enter the good land — but enemies lived there, so they had to FIGHT for it.
Fighting a whole land takes a huge, coordinated ARMY — not a one-person job!
God told Moses to NUMBER everyone by their families and their fathers’ households.
Each tribe camped around the tabernacle, on four sides, all FACING the tent where God dwelt.
It wasn’t their choice where to camp — it was GOD’s, and it was a wonderful, orderly arrangement.
We can accept where God has placed us — in our family and among His people!
lastWeekReview.discussion: Did you thank God for YOUR family this week — even the hard parts — and obey your parents in one thing without grumbling? Share how it went, soldier in God’s army!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “…of whom every family in the heavens and on earth is named.” — Ephesians 3:14-15

kidsContent.text: Israel had been numbered and formed into an army. Now they were getting CLOSE to the good land God promised — Canaan!
But how would millions of people know which way to go? There was no map and no GPS — and they didn’t need one!
God dwelt among them in the tabernacle, and a CLOUD covered it. That cloud was their guide!
When the cloud lifted and moved, Israel moved. When the cloud settled, they stopped and camped.
🌟 Because they followed the cloud — God’s word to them — even millions of people stayed in perfect order, together by family and tribe!

image.caption: The pillar of cloud guiding Israel through the wilderness

kidsContent.text: Israel didn’t set out whenever they felt like it, or only when the weather looked nice. They moved when GOD moved — they trusted His leading.
God still guides us today. Not with a cloud, but through the older ones He gives us: our parents, our serving ones, and those who follow Him.
We don’t have to figure out everything on our own! God will show us where to go, when to move, and when to wait.
🌟 This week, let’s follow our “cloud” — the parents and serving ones God has placed over us to guide us in His way!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, follow your “cloud”! When your parents or a serving one guides you where to go or what to do, obey cheerfully and right away — trusting that God is leading you through them.

memoryVerse.text: But it is Jehovah who is going before you. He will be with you; He will not fail you nor forsake you. Do not fear, neither be dismayed.
memoryVerse.application: Wherever God leads, He goes FIRST! He never leaves us or lets us down — so we don’t need to be afraid. We can follow His leading (through our parents and serving ones) with confidence.

activity.title: ☁️ Follow the Cloud — Move When God Moves

parts.text: Materials: A “cloud” (a white balloon, a cotton-ball sign, or a white cloth on a stick), and open space with a few “camp” spots marked on the floor.
Setup: One leader holds the cloud. The children are the tribes of Israel, ready to journey. Remind them: we only move when the cloud moves!
Round 1 — Watch the Cloud: When the leader raises and moves the cloud, everyone marches together behind it. When the leader lowers the cloud, everyone stops and “makes camp” (sits down) right away.
Round 2 — Stay Together: The cloud speeds up, slows down, turns, and stops at different “camps.” Tribes must stay together and follow — nobody runs ahead on their own idea!
Round 3 — Tricky Cloud: The leader pretends to move but doesn’t, or lowers the cloud suddenly. Anyone who moves on their own (instead of watching the cloud) sits out one turn.
📖 Connection: Israel moved only when God’s cloud moved. We follow our “cloud” — our parents and serving ones — instead of our own feet!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: The Israelite camp in the wilderness. Tents everywhere. Two young Israelites, Eli and Dinah, are playing when a horn sounds.
For years God led His people through the wilderness. A cloud rested over the tabernacle. When it moved, everyone moved. When it stopped, everyone stopped.
Dinah, look! The cloud is lifting off the tabernacle! Do you know what that means?
It’s time to pack up and move again! Awww — but I just built the BEST fort behind our tent!
I know… I wanted to go explore that big hill over there. But the cloud isn’t going to the hill.
Children, roll up the mats — quickly now! We follow the cloud, not our own feet.
But Mother, why can’t we choose where to go? I want to stay HERE.
Because God is our Guide. The cloud shows us the way. When we follow it, our whole family stays together and safe.
So the horns blew, the tribes lined up in order, and two million people set out together — following the cloud.
Look — everyone is moving the same way, by families and tribes. Nobody is lost!
Because we’re all following God’s cloud instead of our own ideas. That’s actually kind of amazing.
And that is how God still leads you today — through your parents and serving ones. Follow us, and you are following Him.
The cloud settles over a new place. The people stop and set up camp.
We’ll follow our cloud — our parents and serving ones — wherever God leads!

description.text: Setup: One leader holds a “cloud” (white balloon or cloth on a stick) at the front. All the kids line up behind as the tribes of Israel.
Rules: When the cloud is UP and moving, everyone marches and follows it around the space. When the cloud comes DOWN, everyone freezes and “makes camp” instantly.
Out: Anyone who keeps moving after the cloud stops — or runs ahead of the cloud — does 5 jumping jacks and rejoins the line.
Twist: The cloud changes speed and direction fast! Tribes must stay together and keep watching the cloud, not their friends.
📖 Connection: Israel moved only when God’s cloud moved. We watch our “cloud” and follow — we don’t go our own way!
Materials: A white balloon or cloth on a stick, open space
Setup: Split into two “tribes.” Each tribe picks one leader to be their “cloud.”
Rules: The leader travels an obstacle path (cones, hops, crawls, spins). Each tribe must copy their leader’s exact moves, in order, staying together.
Scoring: A tribe scores only if EVERYONE followed the leader’s path correctly — speed doesn’t help if you break away and do your own thing.
Switch: Rotate leaders each round so everyone gets to lead and to follow.
📖 Connection: Following a good leader keeps the whole group together and safe — just like following God’s cloud!
Materials: Cones or floor markers, open space
Choose one leader to be the “cloud.” Everyone else follows in a line as the tribes on the journey.
Goal: Only the cloud chooses the path — over the log, around the tree, along the fence. Followers may not shortcut or wander off to their own spot.
Rule: When the cloud stops and sits, everyone stops and “makes camp.” When the cloud rises, the journey continues.
Finish: Gather at the final “camp” and thank God that He always shows us the way to go.
Materials: Just an open outdoor space with a few natural landmarks

outdoor.tip: ☁️ The lesson is guidance: God leads His people, and He still guides us through our parents and serving ones. Help the kids feel the joy and safety of following, instead of running off on their own ideas.
